title: Many-to-one — multiple items per zone
description: Verifies the `multipleItemsPerZone: true` configuration: each zone accepts MORE than one item, and a zone is correct only when its placed set exactly matches `accepts`.

data.markdown: By default, a DragMatch zone accepts exactly one item. Setting `multipleItemsPerZone: true` flips the contract: a zone accepts as many items as its `accepts` array lists, and the zone is correct when its placed set exactly equals `accepts`. Order within a zone does not matter.

data.prompt: Drop each language into the paradigm zone it most belongs to.
data.explanation: Haskell, OCaml, and Elixir lead with functional semantics. C, Go, and Rust are imperative systems languages. Prolog is the canonical logic-programming language. Many real languages mix paradigms — this exercise picks the dominant one.
